nodes.title: fix: keep question mark segments out of the base directory (#380)
nodes.body:
### What is the purpose of this pull request?

Fixes #380: patterns with `?` in a directory segment can start traversal from a literal, nonexistent directory and return no matches.

```js
fg.sync('?/test'); // [] instead of ['a/test']
fg.sync('fi?st/file.md', { cwd: 'fixtures' }); // [] instead of ['first/file.md']
```

### What changes did you make?

Normalize unescaped `?` to `*` only for `glob-parent`'s base extraction. The original pattern is still used for matching, so `?` continues to match exactly one character. Escaped characters and Windows device prefixes are preserved. `glob-parent` continues to handle roots, other wildcard segments, and unescaping.

### Why adapt this in fast-glob?

`is-glob` deliberately excludes bare `?` in strict mode, while fast-glob documents it as a wildcard. The existing upstream proposal, [micromatch/is-glob#12](https://github.com/micromatch/is-glob/pull/12), remains open. Its maintainer [explicitly directed the fix toward del or fast-glob](https://github.com/micromatch/is-glob/pull/12#issuecomment-801495613), preserving that strict-mode behavior. The related discussion is [gulpjs/glob-parent#39](https://github.com/gulpjs/glob-parent/issues/39).

With the current dependencies (`glob-parent` 6.0.2 and `is-glob` 4.0.3), `isGlob('?/test')` is still false and `globParent('?/test')` is still `'?'`. This adapter aligns traversal with fast-glob's matching semantics without changing either dependency's public behavior.

### Validation

Added unit coverage for leading and nested `?` segments, escaping, absolute roots, earlier wildcard segments, escaped backslashes, and Windows device prefixes. Added end-to-end cases for sync, async, and stream matching against existing fixtures.

Updated against current master and ran `npm run build` and `SNAPSHOT_SKIP_PRUNING=1 npm run test:e2e` on macOS. Build, lint, unit tests, and all enabled end-to-end tests pass. Windows-only filesystem cases remain for upstream CI.

Closes #380.

nodes.title: fix: use basename for `name` field of static-pattern entries in object mode
nodes.body:
## Problem

Fixes #487.

With `objectMode: true`, entries produced from a **static** pattern (e.g. `./package.json`)
expose `name` equal to the whole pattern string, while entries produced from a **dynamic**
pattern (e.g. `./*.json`) expose `name` equal to the real basename, as documented in the
README ("name (`string`) — the last part of the path (basename)"). This makes the shape of
the returned entry, and of `entry.dirent.name`, inconsistent depending on how a match was
found, even though both point at the same file.

Empirical reproduction (Node v22.23.1, built `out/`, see counterfactual section below):

```
STATIC (./package.json):
[ { name: './package.json', path: './package.json', dirent: DirentFromStats { name: './package.json', ... } } ]

DYNAMIC (./*.json) -> package.json entry:
[ { dirent: Dirent { name: 'package.json', ... }, name: 'package.json', path: 'package.json' } ]
```

## Root cause

`src/readers/reader.ts:35-41`, `Reader#_makeEntry`:

```ts
protected _makeEntry(stats: FsStats, pattern: Pattern): Entry {
	const entry: Entry = {
		name: pattern,
		path: pattern,
		dirent: utils.fs.createDirentFromStats(pattern, stats),
	};
	...
```

This method backs the static-pattern path only (`ReaderStream#static` in
`src/readers/stream.ts`, used by both `ReaderSync#static` and `ReaderAsync#static`). It uses
the raw `pattern` string for both `name` and the synthetic `Dirent`'s `name`, instead of
deriving the basename. The dynamic path (`Reader#dynamic`) delegates to `@nodelib/fs.walk`,
which already returns real `fs.Dirent` entries with a correct basename `name`, so the two
code paths silently diverged.

## Fix

`src/readers/reader.ts`: derive the basename once with `path.basename(pattern)` and use it
for both `entry.name` and the name passed into `createDirentFromStats`. `entry.path` is left
untouched (still the full pattern, matching existing behavior and the dynamic path's `path`
semantics).

```ts
protected _makeEntry(stats: FsStats, pattern: Pattern): Entry {
	const name = path.basename(pattern);
	const entry: Entry = {
		name,
		path: pattern,
		dirent: utils.fs.createDirentFromStats(name, stats),
	};
	...
```

No changes to `src/utils/fs.ts`: `createDirentFromStats(name, stats)` was already generic;
only the caller passed the wrong value.

## Test

Added a regression test in `src/readers/reader.spec.ts` (`.makeEntry` suite) using a pattern
with a directory part (`./directory/config.json`), asserting `entry.name` and
`entry.dirent.name` are the basename `config.json` while `entry.path` stays the full pattern.
The pre-existing test in the same suite uses a bare `config.json` pattern (no directory
component), so it does not change under the fix (basename of a bare filename is itself) and
still passes.

Fix Windows rooted absolute exclusions so matching positive and negative patterns cancel with or without a drive letter. Fixes #486.

Resolve only the root of single-slash Windows negative patterns against `cwd`, preserving glob syntax and explicit drive/UNC roots. Add regression coverage and clarify the Windows pattern documentation.

<summary>Implementation and validation</summary>

Absolute negative patterns were compiled without a drive while candidate paths were resolved to drive-qualified paths. Prefixing only the escaped filesystem root reconciles these forms without passing glob expressions through `path.resolve`.

nodes.title: fix: read the root of a drive for patterns like C:/* on Windows
nodes.body:
### What is the purpose of this pull request?

Fixes #375. On Windows, a pattern for the root of a drive, such as `C:/*`, lists the current working directory instead of the drive root.

`glob-parent` returns `C:` as the base directory of `C:/*` (gulpjs/glob-parent#63). Windows resolves a drive letter without a separator to the current directory on that drive, so `path.resolve(cwd, 'C:')` is the cwd. The entries found there are then reported under the drive, for example `C:/src` for the repository's own `src` directory. `C:/./*` already works because its base is `C:/.`.

### What changes did you make? (Give an overview)

- `groupPatternsByBaseDirectory` now keeps the trailing slash when the base is a bare drive letter taken from a `X:/…` pattern, so the base of `C:/*` is `C:/`, the same way `/*` gets `/`. This only applies on Windows. On other platforms `C:` is an ordinary relative directory name, so nothing changes there.
- The check is a small helper in `utils/path` next to `appendTrailingSeparatorToDeviceRoot`, and it runs after `getBaseDirectory` rather than inside it.
- Tests:
  - A unit test for the helper.
  - A grouping test in `managers/tasks.spec.ts`.
  - A `globSync` test that uses a custom `fs.readdirSync` to check that the drive root is the directory being read.

### What is the purpose of this pull request?

For example, with `cwd` beneath `build.local`, `ignore: ['**/*.local/**']` can discard a file merely because that ancestor matches. nodes.title: fix(readers): use the basename as the name of static entries
nodes.body:
### What is the purpose of this pull request?

Fixes #487.

With `objectMode` (or `stats`), an entry found by a static pattern uses the whole pattern as its `name` and `dirent.name`. The README documents `name` as "the last part of the path (basename)", and dynamic patterns already return the basename:

```js
fg.globSync('packages/a/package.json', { objectMode: true })[0].name; // 'packages/a/package.json'
fg.globSync('packages/*/package.json', { objectMode: true })[0].name; // 'package.json'
```

An absolute static pattern returns the whole absolute path as the name.

### What changes did you make? (Give an overview)

`Reader._makeEntry` now uses `path.basename(pattern)` for `name` and for the name of the `DirentFromStats`. `path` is unchanged, so string results and the `absolute`, `markDirectories`, `stats` and filter behavior stay the same; the library code does not read `entry.name`. A static pattern for the filesystem root (`/`) now gets an empty name, which is what `path.basename('/')` returns.

Tests: a `Reader` unit test with a nested pattern, and `globSync`, `glob` and `globStream` tests in `src/index.spec.ts` that compare static and dynamic matches of `fixtures/first/file.md`. All four fail without the change.

Lint, compile, unit tests and the sync, async and stream e2e suites pass on Linux with Node 22.13.0, 22, 24 and 26. A fresh `npm install` currently resolves `@types/sinon` 22.0.1 (published 2026-10-21), which makes `tsc` fail on `master` as well (`SinonStub` is no longer exported; 24 errors in the reader and provider specs), so I ran the checks with `@types/sinon@22.0.0`. nodes.title: Preserve negative basename patterns with baseNameMatch
nodes.body:
### What is the purpose of this pull request?

Preserve negative patterns when `baseNameMatch` adds a globstar prefix. Given `a.txt`, `b.txt`, `nested/a.txt` and `nested/b.txt`, this call currently returns all four files:

```js
fg.globSync(['*.txt', '!a.txt'], { cwd, baseNameMatch: true });
```

It should return only `b.txt` and `nested/b.txt`, matching `ignore: ['a.txt']`. The same bug affects the async and stream APIs, and negated entries in `ignore`.
